speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing; please note that while I cannot speak directly to you, your parents or caregivers should answer the following questions on your behalf. To start, what is your exact age, and have you noticed that these breathing difficulties worsen specifically when you feed or lie down?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Tracheomalacia (specifically laryngotracheomalacia).

The clinical picture of stridor and wheezing that worsens with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, combined with post-feeding vomiting, is highly characteristic of tracheomalacia. Do you have any records of a previous flexible laryngoscopy or bronchoscopy performed? If not, would you like me to request images of the airway or order a chest X-ray to confirm the diagnosis?
